overview: Cross-sectional survey of adults receiving systemic cancer therapy at four day units over three months.
population: Consecutive adults attending for systemic therapy on sampled clinic days from February to April 2027; one questionnaire per person.
exposure: Age, household income, employment change, travel distance, therapy type and benefits status.
procedures: The coordinator samples clinic days at random, approaches every eligible patient, records age, sex and postcode of everyone approached, and offers paper, tablet or telephone completion in four languages with interpreters.

outcomes.name: Moderate or severe financial toxicity
outcomes.measure: Score in the moderate or severe range on the validated 11-item questionnaire

outcomes.name: Out-of-pocket spending
outcomes.measure: Self-reported spending on travel, parking and medicines in the previous month

outcomes.name: Response by group
outcomes.measure: Completed questionnaires divided by patients approached, by age, language and distance
outcomes.why: Non-response hides the most affected (claim c3).

feasibility: About 1,200 eligible attenders in three months at two coordinator days a week on sampled clinic days.

biasFlags.label: Non-response among the most affected
biasFlags.note: Weighted estimates reported alongside crude ones.

biasFlags.label: Survivor sampling
biasFlags.note: Patients who stopped treatment are not approached.

parsimony.simplestPath: One questionnaire, one primary outcome, one weighted prevalence.

summary: Survey of all adults on systemic therapy with one primary outcome.
